bull_bear.body:
- Core SGF (Settlement Guarantee Fund) stands at ₹1,444 Cr — disclosed both in the quarter highlights and under MCXCCL.
- MCXCCL paid-up share capital is ₹239.99 Cr, with 10 clearing banks empanelled and 248 clearing members.
- Shares outstanding are 254.99 MN; BSE market capitalisation is stated at ₹723.40 Bn with a 52-week high/low of ₹3,480 / ₹1,461 as on June 30, 2026 (NSE capitalisation marked "NA").
- The deck states no dividend, buyback or reinvestment policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Deck states "MCX continues to command over 99% share across bullion, base metals and energy"; the futures turnover mix for Q1 FY27 shows Gold 34.5%, Silver 29.7%, Crude Oil 16.6%, Natural Gas 8.8%, Copper 7.7%, Aluminium 1.4%, Zinc 1.1%, Other 0.1%, with the deck's own callout "Gold + Silver = 77% of Futures Turnover".
- Corporate & governance moat claimed: "India's first listed exchange", "Member of IOSCO", and a "Board & top-management refresh"; journey markers are Incorporated 2002, Operations begin 2003, MCXCCL clearing live 2018, New CDP platform 2023, "Record scale" 2025-26.
- MCXCCL is described as a 100% subsidiary of MCX, in operations since Sept 3, 2018, and "central counterparty for all trades executed on MCX" — the deck calls it "India's First Commodity Clearing Corporation".
- Global linkages cited: licensing with LME, NYMEX (CME Group) and IEX; an MoU with CME Group; consultancy for Bangladesh's first exchange; and joining other MIIs to set up IIBX, GIFT City.
- Regulatory tailwinds listed as structural: bank-sponsored broking entities permitted, banks allowed as Professional Clearing Members, member-level fungibility, mutual funds via hybrid schemes, Portfolio Managers permitted, and FPIs cleared to trade with DMA extended.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ownership framework] SEBI-driven investment criteria constrain the register: all shareholders must be "fit and proper" at all times, prior SEBI approval is needed to acquire beyond 5%, at least 51% must be held by the public, trading members & associates are capped at 49% in aggregate, and foreign exchanges/depositories/banks/insurers may hold up to 15%.
- [Shareholding] As on June 30, 2026: Mutual Funds 30.07%, FPIs 29.84%, Resident Individuals 15.83%, Banks 15.00%, QIB 4.77%, Bodies Corporate 1.87%, Others 2.62%; the largest single holder is Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd at 14.99% — effectively at the 15% foreign/bank-type ceiling context the deck describes.
- [Risk & certifications] MCXCCL runs a SPAN-based value-at-risk margining model and an Electronic Warehouse Receipts System (non-agri in-house, agri via CCRL), and holds ISO 27001:2022, ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 22301:2019, with membership of the Asia-Pacific CSD Group and primary membership of CCP12.
- [Leadership] Ms. Praveena Rai is MD & CEO (former COO of NPCI); the deck lists two Executive Directors (Sanjay Rajpal — Critical Operations; Manoj Jain — Regulatory, Compliance, Risk Management & Investor Grievances) and a Chairman who is a Public Interest Director, Dr. Harsh Kumar Bhanwala.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions MCX as "India's Leading Commodity Derivatives Exchange" — India's first listed exchange, IOSCO member and owner of the country's first commodity clearing corporation (MCXCCL) — commanding "over 99% share across bullion, base metals and energy" with a book now dominated by options on bullion and energy.

open.item: SGF-related cost (including 1% ISF/IPF) around 7% of transaction income; ~5% recurring SGF portion expected to persist as volumes grow.
New products roadmap (electricity futures, index options) fully ready technically and go-to-market; awaiting final regulatory approvals, believed to be around the corner.
FY26 tech cost expected around INR90-110 crores and employee cost INR150-160 crores (directionally around FY25 levels).
Depreciation/amortization expected to continue at current levels; overall expense ratios expected to stay flat in FY26 (no specific capex number given).
Base metal volumes roughly doubled in FY25; working with industry to relax mutual-fund/DII restrictions to participate in commodity derivatives.
SEBI consultation paper on segregating clearing corporations from exchanges flagged; management does not expect it to apply to commodity CCL any time soon given warehouse/delivery complexity.
Index options (BULLDEX, METLDEX) will be cash-settled options on the index itself (not on index futures), in advanced testing stage.
Planning to launch silver monthly/micro options (30 kg, 5 kg, 1 kg) in the shorter time frame; no definite date.
Management confident of reviving the nickel contract (currently dead), though contract changes not yet defined; remains on radar.
Effective tax rate expected to remain in the range of 21% to 23% for near and medium term.
Board approved investment in India International Bullion Holdings (IIBH, Gold Spot Exchange associate, 20% stake); IIBH contributed INR42.7 lakh to MCX P&L this quarter.
Technology cost expected to be similar to earlier base plus depreciation, a few percentage points higher or lower, barring additional regulatory infra investments.
Steel TMT contract traction is not encouraging yet in its first month; expected to take time to mature and be self-sustaining in a few years.
Signed MoU with mjunction to set up a coal spot exchange; sought in-principle regulatory approval, actively engaged with ministry.
Management expects to recover a substantial part of what was paid to prior vendor 63 Moons, via pending TCS post-go-live activities settlement.
Incremental annual depreciation from the INR237 cr capitalization will be in the range of INR30-35 crores.
Own co-location infrastructure depends on regulatory enablement; MCX will provide for it when regulators permit co-location in commodities.
GST registration requirements across multiple delivery-centre states are deterring participants from taking delivery, flagged as a growth constraint.
Strategic push to make a multi-product attempt to penetrate India's under-developed commodity markets and increase hedger participation.
Empanelling more spot polling players to get maximum reach before arriving at spot prices to improve transparency.
